questions.question: Which inert gas is used in double-glazed windows to fill the space between the panes?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Argon is a chemical element with the atomic number 18.

 
 
• It is a Nobel gas.
 
• It is in group 18 of the periodic table.
 
• Argon is the third most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere (0.094%)
 
• Uses: Fluorescent Lightning, Gas Discharge Tubes, Fluorescent Glow Starters.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It was discovered by William Ramsay and Morris Travers in 1898.
 
• It is more than 4.5 times heavier than air.
 
• xenon is colorless, odorless, and tasteless.

• All these are gases and chemically unreactive.
 
• They form very few compounds.
 
• Because of this they are termed noble gases.

• Xenon and radon are the rarest elements of the group.

• Helium gas is used to inflate party balloons, scientific balloons and blimps etc.

questions.question: How many Mahajanapadas were there during the age of Buddha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**16**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the lifetime of Lord Gautam Buddha, 16 great powers (Mahajanpadas) existed in the 7th and early 6th centuries BC.
 
• These were Kasi, Kosala, Anga, Magadha, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Machcha, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara and Kamboja.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Buddha was born in BC 563 in Lumbini (near the Indo-Nepal Border) and died at the age of eighty in BC 483 at Kushinagar in UP.
 
• At the age of 29, Gautama left home and rejected his life of riches and embraced a lifestyle of asceticism.
 
• After 49 consecutive days of meditation, Gautama attained enlightenment under a pipal tree (Bodhi Tree) at Bodhgaya a village in Bihar.
 
• Buddha gave his first sermon in the village of Sarnath in UP. This event is known as Dharma-Chakra-Pravartana.

 
• **Buddhist Councils marked important turning points in early Buddhism, In total, 4 major Buddhist councils were convened-** 

 
 
• The First Council was held soon after the Mahaparinirvan of the Buddha, around 483 BC in the Sattapani cave at Rajgriha. 
 
• The second Council was held in 383 BC in Vaishali.
 
• The third council was held in 250 BC in Patliputra.
 
• The fourth Council was held in 1st century AD at Kundalvana, Kashmir.

questions.question: Which of the following is expressed as the total number of deaths per thousand population per year in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Death Rate**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A mortality rate is the number of deaths during a particular period of time among a particular type or group of people.

 
 
• It is also called the Death Rate, that measured as the number of deaths per thousand persons in a year.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The number of newborn deaths per 1,000 live births is known as the infant mortality rate.
 
• The infant mortality rate is an essential indicator of a society's general health, in addition to providing crucial information regarding maternal and baby health.
 
• The crude mortality rate is derived by dividing the number of fatalities in a particular time by the number of people who were at risk of dying during that period.
 
• A death rate that is limited to a certain age group is known as an age-specific mortality rate.

• **Apoptosis**, or programmed cell death, is a controlled process by which cells undergo self-destruction.
 
• This is crucial for maintaining health by eliminating damaged or unnecessary cells.

• They release **cytochrome c** into the cytosol, which then triggers the activation of caspases (proteins that execute apoptosis).

• **Some proteins from the Golgi may also play a role in regulating apoptosis indirectly.**
 
• It is **central to processes like the production of lysosomes **and glycosylation of proteins.
 
 
 
• **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)**
 
 
• The **ER is responsible for the synthesis of proteins (rough ER) and lipids (smooth ER), as well as detoxification processes.**
 
• The** ER plays a crucial role in the unfolded protein respons**e (UPR) and ER stress-induced apoptosis.

• **Lysosomes are involved in autophagy,** a process that can promote cell survival or death, depending on the context.

**Calculation:**

LCM of 7 and 11:

7 and 11 are prime numbers.

LCM(7, 11) = 7 × 11 = 77

Now, we need to find how many multiples of 77 are less than 1,000.

Number of multiples of 77 less than 1,000 = ⌊1000 / 77⌋

⇒ ⌊1000 / 77⌋ = ⌊12.987…⌋

Since we take the floor value, we get 12.

**Therefore, the number of numbers less than 1,000 that are multiples of both 7 and 11 is 12.**

questions.question: Four numbers are in the ratio of 2 : 3 : 4 : 5, and their sum is 56. Find the sum of the first and third numbers.

Sum of the numbers in ratio = Sum of the ratios × Common multiple

Let the common multiple be x.

The numbers are 2x, 3x, 4x, and 5x.

Sum of the numbers: 2x + 3x + 4x + 5x = 56
